application_guidance.input_pattern: An exact monotone VI with a verified joint Euclidean Lipschitz bound and an existing solution.
read_original_when: Comparing this local statement with printed Theorem 1 or transferring to another norm, Oracle or infinite-dimensional space.
sensitive_conditions: Finite dimension is used to obtain a norm-convergent subsequence.
Eta is fixed and eta L_T<1; the endpoint eta=1/L_T is not covered.
Monotonicity, exact projections and exact feedback are used in the proof.
For a saddle application, separately verify the VI equivalence, monotonicity and the actual joint constant; do not silently equate it with a block constant.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Deterministic one-step inequality and asymptotic whole-sequence convergence.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: The displayed residual coefficient is exactly 1-eta²L_T² and the bound depends on the initial distance to the chosen solution.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact F evaluation at x_k and y_k; exact P_C.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Main iterates converge in Euclidean norm; trial residual has the displayed square-summability bound. No claim about an unrestricted Oracle model.
complexity_scope.regime: Finite d; fixed eta with eta L_T<1; k->infinity.
complexity_scope.resource: Two F evaluations and two C projections per iteration, separately charged; vector arithmetic O(d). No finite solution-distance or gap accuracy call bound is claimed.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Only the exact fixed-step projected extragradient recurrence displayed in this statement.

content.intended_use: Provide a precisely scoped local convergence argument for the existing joint-L adapter.

proofs.full_local_argument: Projection facts: For any a in R^d, minimizing ||a-v||² over nonempty closed convex C has a minimizer because a minimizing sequence can be restricted to a closed bounded ball, which is compact in finite dimension. Strict convexity of squared distance gives uniqueness. If p=P_C(a), differentiating ||a-(p+t(v-p))||² at t=0+ gives <a-p,v-p><=0 for each v in C. Conversely this inequality implies ||a-v||²=||a-p||²+||v-p||²-2<a-p,v-p>>=||a-p||², so it characterizes p. It also gives ||p-z||²<=||a-z||²-||a-p||² for z in C. For p=P_C(a), r=P_C(b), applying the characterization with v=r and v=p and adding yields ||p-r||²<=<a-b,p-r><=||a-b||||p-r||; hence P_C is 1-Lipschitz. Fix x in C and z* in Sol(F,C), and put p=P_C(x-eta F(x)), q=P_C(x-eta F(p)). Applying the preceding squared projection inequality to q and z* and expanding gives ||q-z*||²<=||x-z*||²-||x-q||²+2eta<F(p),z*-q>. Monotonicity and the VI give <F(p),p-z*>=<F(p)-F(z*),p-z*>+<F(z*),p-z*>>=0. Thus the right side is at most ||x-z*||²-||x-q||²+2eta<F(p),p-q>. Since x-q=(x-p)+(p-q), expand the square to obtain ||q-z*||²<=||x-z*||²-||x-p||²-||p-q||²+2<x-p,q-p>-2eta<F(p),q-p>. The projection characterization at p with v=q gives <x-p,q-p><=eta<F(x),q-p>. Substitution yields ||q-z*||²<=||x-z*||²-||x-p||²-||p-q||²+2eta<F(x)-F(p),q-p>. The last inner product term is at most 2eta L_T||x-p||||q-p||, which is at most eta²L_T²||x-p||²+||q-p||² because (eta L_T||x-p||-||q-p||)²>=0. Cancellation proves the displayed one-step inequality. Set c=1-eta²L_T²>0. Applied at each iteration, it shows that ||x_k-z*|| is nonincreasing, hence x_k is bounded. Summing from k=0 to N gives c sum_{k=0}^N ||x_k-y_k||²<=||x_0-z*||²-||x_{N+1}-z*||²<=||x_0-z*||². Nonnegative partial sums therefore converge, so ||x_k-y_k||->0. Finite-dimensional boundedness gives a subsequence x_{k_j}->zbar; closedness of C gives zbar in C, and the residual limit gives y_{k_j}->zbar. Lipschitz continuity of F and continuity of P_C then allow passing to the limit in y_{k_j}=P_C(x_{k_j}-eta F(x_{k_j})), yielding zbar=P_C(zbar-eta F(zbar)). Its projection characterization is <-eta F(zbar),v-zbar><=0 for every v in C; division by eta>0 proves zbar in Sol(F,C). Apply the established one-step inequality with this fixed zbar. The nonnegative distances ||x_k-zbar|| form a nonincreasing sequence with a subsequence tending to zero, so their full limit is zero. Finally ||y_k-zbar||<=||y_k-x_k||+||x_k-zbar||->0. Every asserted conclusion follows.
proofs.locator: Local reconstruction inspired by printed pp.38–40 Eq.(7)–(16); the argument below is local mathematical content, not a source quotation.
map: Use the two projection inequalities, monotonicity and joint Lipschitz continuity for the squared-distance bound.
Telescope, extract a finite-dimensional cluster point, identify it by projection optimality, and use Fejer monotonicity for whole-sequence convergence.
proofs.omitted_details: None for the local statement; standard finite-dimensional compactness and elementary differentiation of squared distance are explicitly used. No external unreviewed scientific dependency is required.
proofs.reading_coverage: Actual original-page inspection of PDF pages 3–6, including the source projection mechanism and convergence argument. The full argument here is separately reconstructed local content.

assumptions: C subset R^d is nonempty, closed and convex.
F:C->R^d is single-valued and monotone: <F(u)-F(v),u-v>>=0 for all u,v in C.
A specified L_T>0 satisfies ||F(u)-F(v)||<=L_T||u-v|| for all u,v in C.
Sol(F,C) is nonempty; all evaluations and projections are exact.
The step eta is constant and satisfies 0<eta<1/L_T.
statement.conclusion: For every k and every solution z*, ||x_{k+1}-z*||² <= ||x_k-z*||²-(1-eta²L_T²)||x_k-y_k||². Consequently sum_{k=0}^infinity ||x_k-y_k||² <= ||x_0-z*||²/(1-eta²L_T²), ||x_k-y_k||->0, and x_k->zbar in Sol(F,C); also y_k->zbar.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Work in R^d with the Euclidean inner product and norm. P_C is exact Euclidean projection. Define Sol(F,C)={z in C: <F(z),v-z>>=0 for every v in C}. Given x_0 in C, define y_k=P_C(x_k-eta F(x_k)) and x_{k+1}=P_C(x_k-eta F(y_k)).
statement.parameter_domains: d in the positive integers, L_T>0, eta in (0,1/L_T), k nonnegative integer. C may be unbounded; no strong monotonicity is assumed.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every finite positive integer d, every C,F,L_T meeting these assumptions, every permitted fixed eta and every x_0 in C, the one-step inequality holds for every k>=0 and every z* in Sol(F,C). There exists zbar in Sol(F,C), depending on the instance and initialization, such that the whole sequence converges to zbar. No randomness.
